sentences.text: Good morning.

You have four stories today: Nvidia pausing chip shipments to Southeast Asia, EvolveMAS, a memory framework for decentralized multi-agent systems, procedure memory for learning recruiter decisions, and OpenAI's claimed proof that the matrix multiplication exponent ω is exactly 9/4.
First, the biggest story this morning.
Nvidia has told its server partners to pause shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.
TechCrunch, citing the Wall Street Journal, reports that Dell and Super Micro were among the manufacturing partners told to hold those shipments.
Nvidia has told manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to those countries for an unspecified period while it assesses whether regional partners meet U.S. export requirements.
The U.S. Commerce Department closed that loophole earlier this month.
The Institute for Progress estimates those remote data centers supply about 24 percent of China's AI computing power.
I can walk you through how that remote access worked, if you want the details.
Next, something for your work on agent memory.
A paper called EvolveMAS addresses decentralized multi-agent systems, where large language model agents interact without centralized control.
Each main agent gets a dedicated MemoryAgent that manages its memory outside the agent's own reasoning context.
Across five benchmarks, EvolveMAS posted the highest normalized average score of 77.2 among the methods compared.
Since you follow agent memory, the dedicated memory agent is the part to watch.
Also on agent memory, a paper on learning recruiter decisions.
Hiring assistants have to infer recruiter preferences that shift across projects and over time.
The authors introduce Procedure Memory, which learns reusable decision steps from past episodes.
On PersonaMem-v2, that approach reached 50.2 percent accuracy, compared with 29.0 percent with no memory.
It also used 69 percent fewer context tokens than keeping the full conversation history.
I can tell you how the memory retrieval works, if you're curious.
And finally, one from outside your usual beat.
OpenAI reportedly claims to have proved that the exponent of matrix multiplication is exactly 9/4.
Scott Aaronson's blog describes that as a lower bound matching an upper bound OpenAI proved earlier.
Yupan Liu also posted an arXiv preprint proving that two-message quantum interactive protocols have the full power of PSPACE.
Which of these would you like to dig into?
